messages:
Incident Bot: pagerduty: page fired -> synth-canary-eu-throttle (threshold: 95th pct latency > 350ms)
PagerDuty: Alert: synth-canary-eu-throttle is firing (x18 incidents in 3m) :rotating_light:
Alex: Saw the PD flood. Lots of repeats — looks like the probe is getting throttled and retrying.
Samira: On it. Any customer impact flags? Console graphs show probe errors but host metrics look ok.
Mike (oncall): I see 5 targets returning 429 from the prober cluster, also a sharp spike in egress from prober-pool-3.
Irene: 429s could be due to rate-limiter kicking in after a bad rollout? We pushed a small canary for routing yesterday.
Alex: Can we silence noisy PD alerts while we investigate? I'll add a 30m maintenance window and annotate.
PagerDuty: Incident suppressed by Alex for 30m. Escalations paused.
Samira: Quick check: `kubectl logs prober-3 | tail -n 200` shows repeated `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and backoff attempts: ```2026-03-14T16:02:01Z prober: request id=abc123 target=eu-west-1 status=429 retrying after=1200ms```
Mike (oncall): Replayed synthetic traffic manually to a single host, behavior reproduces. Throttle header present: `X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 1` every other request.
Irene: If the new routing policy is causing fanout to the same shard, that could trigger the per-target limiter. Any recent routing config changes?
Alex: Yes, routing-change PR #4463 merged 9h ago; it adjusts sticky hashing to reduce cross-region churn. Could be mis-hashing causing hotspots.
Samira: Plan: 1) pause canary routing-rollout 2) temporarily increase per-target limiter to absorb burst 3) silence PD (done) 4) open follow-up for routing revert if needed.
Mike (oncall): Executing step 1 now: `svcctl rollback routing-change --canary-id=rc-4463` — returning canary to previous traffic split.
Incident Bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started (job id: rb-29321).
Samira: Step 2: bump limiter on prober nodes: `andrew@infra:/home$ airflow run limiter.scale --service=prober --limit=1000` — patch applied to prober-pool-*.
Irene: Patch applied on all 6 nodes. Monitoring latency and 429 rate.
Alex: PV graphs: 429s dropped by 90% within 45s of the limiter bump. Retry spikes subsiding.
Mike (oncall): PagerDuty suppression still active. Recommend extend to 60m to avoid noisy repeats while we validate.
PagerDuty: Alex extended maintenance window to 60m.
Samira: Still seeing a residual spike in prober-pool-1 — investigating logs for any downstream 503s.
Irene: Found `upstream: backend-eu-3` returning 503 intermittently at the same times as probe retries. Might be partial backend degradation triggering retries which then tripped limiter.
Alex: Good find. I'll route around backend-eu-3 via traffic-shift: `routerctl set-weight backend-eu-3=0.0` for 5m.
Incident Bot: router-bot: weight update applied to backend-eu-3 (previous 0.2 -> 0.0).
Mike (oncall): After routing change, probe errors drop to near-zero. Dashboard latency back to normal.
Samira: Recommend leaving routing change until next deploy window and opening a ticket for backend-eu-3 investigation (possible OOM or autoscale misfire).
Irene: Created ticket INF-2026 with logs and heap dump request to the owning service team.
Alex: TL;DR: Not a global outage, localized backend flapping created retries that hit per-target rate-limiter, which caused a PD storm. Mitigations: limiter bump + rollback canary + route-away backend.
Mike (oncall): Handing off to Samira for post-incident follow-up. I'm going offline in 25m.
Samira: I'll take it. Action items: 1) PD suppression review (audit why repeated alerts weren't de-duplicated) 2) routing PR review for hashing edge-case 3) backend-eu-3 auto-scale and memory investigation 4) add prober backoff jitter to reduce synchronized retries.
PagerDuty: Maintenance window ends in 55m (unless extended).
Alex: FYI — I'll add a short postmortem note and link to INF-2026.
Incident Bot: incident-note: initial mitigation actions recorded to INF-2026.
Samira: Closing thread for active mitigation; will reopen if PD fires again. Thanks all :raised_hands:
